title: Penne Puttanesca
subtitle: A bold sauce of tomatoes, anchovies, olives, and capers
excerpt: Puttanesca is a punchy, briny sauce that needs nothing more than pasta and a storecupboard. It comes together in under 20 minutes.
sourceNotes: Neapolitan origins; a pantry sauce that keeps most of its ingredients in tins and jars.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The sauce keeps in the fridge for three days. Reheat gently and toss with freshly cooked pasta.

content.text: Puttanesca is a storecupboard sauce with a lot of flavour for very little work. The anchovies melt into the oil and you barely know they are there, but the sauce would be flat without them. Do not let the garlic colour past pale gold or it will turn bitter.
Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil. Add the penne and cook until 2 minutes short of the packet time.
Warm the olive oil in a wide frying pan over a low heat. Add the garlic, anchovies, and chilli flakes. Cook for 2 minutes, pressing the anchovies with a spoon until they dissolve.
Add the tomatoes. Stir well, turn the heat to medium, and simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce has thickened slightly.
Stir in the olives and capers. Taste before adding any salt as the anchovies and capers are both salty.
Reserve a mug of pasta water, then drain the penne. Tip it into the sauce.
Toss over the heat for 2 minutes, adding pasta water as needed. Scatter with parsley and serve.

items.cause: Salt was added before tasting; anchovies, capers, and olives all carry salt.
items.fix: Always taste the sauce after adding the olives and capers before seasoning. A splash of pasta water or an extra glug of olive oil can help balance it.

items.cause: The heat was too high and the garlic browned before the anchovies dissolved.
items.fix: Use a low heat and keep the garlic moving; it should soften and turn pale, not golden.

items.cause: The tomatoes were not reduced for long enough.
items.fix: Keep simmering with the lid off until the sauce coats a spoon before adding the pasta.
